final.title: Check the process before you automate it
final.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, decide whether the workflow is stable enough to test at all. For an owner-operator, that usually means one repeatable task: customer questions, invoices, or data work. The question is simple: does this task produce the same kind of output most times, or do people quietly handle exceptions in different ways from one week to the next?

If the manual process is inconsistent, automation will not fix it. It will repeat the inconsistency faster. So the better boundary is not “can AI do this?” but “can I describe this process clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?”

A practical next step is to document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human must still check the work. That gives you a real basis for deciding whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. Bareni’s diagnostic approach starts with that kind of workflow check: one recurring process, honest about where it breaks, and clear about whether AI fits.
